subject: beetle
pitch: A proud stag beetle on a mossy log. A glossy chestnut wing case with a mirror shine, a black head and thorax, huge branched antler-like jaws in reddish brown, elbowed antennae with feathery tips, and six spiny black legs gripping the bark. A dewdrop clings to one of its antlers.
reasoning:
I'm working out realistic proportions for the scene—figuring the beetle's size relative to a log, and deciding to orient the log along the Z axis with the beetle facing forward on top of it.

I'm sketching a skeleton hierarchy for the beetle: a root joint, body, head, jaws, antennae chains, legs, and elytra hinges, keeping it manageable in joint count. I'm then working out the foot placement math so legs land correctly on the curved log surface, and planning elytra as scaled sphere halves positioned symmetrically on the body.

Now I'm placing the body segments along the Z-axis—head, thorax, and elytra—sizing each so the beetle reads clearly but doesn't overwhelm the log, and adding a subtle highlight shape to fake a glossy shell since the material system can't do true specular shine.

Setting up joints for the head, jaws, and elytra hinges with their parent bones and directions, then planning how parts attach using scaled sphere geometries for ellipsoid shapes with flat shading for a faceted look.

For the elytra, I'm sizing and positioning the two wing covers slightly overlapping at the seam for a natural groove, using chestnut and highlight tones with small flattened shine streaks, then moving on to shape the thorax as a scaled dark sphere.

Now I'm placing the pronotum plate, abdomen, and head as scaled spheres with appropriate darker colors and positions, adding small bumps for eyes, and sketching curved jaw shapes that sweep outward then taper inward toward the tip using a spline path.

Still writing jaw rig code...

For the dewdrop I'll place a tiny pale blue translucent sphere at the left jaw tine tip, computed from the sweep point plus direction offset, with a small white highlight sphere for shine, bound to the jawTip bone. Then I'm starting on the antennae, building an elbowed chain from a base point near the head front side.

Still refining antenna geometry...

Now moving to legs: planning 6 legs total, three per side, with hip positions defined for the front pair first.

Foot targets need computing against the log's curved surface, offsetting forward for front legs, flat for middle, and back for hind legs, placing feet just above the surface. Each leg uses three segments — femur, tibia, tarsus — with bend directions set so knees point up and out before articulating toward the foot targets.

Checking reach distances for each leg segment confirms the lengths work for front, mid, and hind limbs, so I'll set segment lengths to roughly 0.04, 0.045, and 0.03. Then I'm naming the joint chain (hip, knee, ankle, foot) for each leg, sweeping a tapered black tube along it for the leg shape, and adding small spike details along the tibia.

Adding foot claws...

Now I'm setting up hip placement with nonzero x-offset and coxa lumps, plus defining the log as a bark-textured cylinder using mottled brown paint with grain detail.

Adding cut-end discs and rings...

Then I'm planning moss clumps scattered across the log's top surface using flat stick spheres for texture.

I'll keep it to just a few mushrooms stuck on, and for randomness I should use my own deterministic generator rather than relying on an uncertain rng API, passing a seed only where I'm sure of the signature. For the jaw, I'm sketching out a chain role with named joints along a short curved path, though I need more points to get a proper tip segment.

Jaws swept from a catmull curve with a tapering radius, parented off the head joint, which itself needs to attach to the thorax by name. Legs similarly need their chain parented to the body. For surface detail, I'm considering adding a thin dark seam along the elytra ridge using a capsule or rod primitive, but deciding to skip it to keep things simpler.

Elytra should probably tilt slightly, but I'll skip precise pitch rotation for now. I'm defining hinge joints for the elytra with a role option, and settling the body's root joint order before writing the actual construction code. Checking belly clearance: thorax underside sits around y=0.258 against a log top near 0.24, leaving enough gap for the legs to mount properly underneath.

I'm skipping detailed eye decals and antenna elbow coordinates for now, planning instead to write a helper for vector construction and a simple polyline chain for the antenna with a small sweep radius, bending it outward then forward-inward to form a natural elbowed shape.

Defining spike fan logic...

Then I'll name the leg joints consistently (hipLF, hipRF, etc. across front/mid/hind), add a dorsal spine sweep with small spikes along its length inheriting bone transforms, and finalize the export structure.
